blocks.t: **Objetivo de comunicação (C2):** eu consigo ler, ouvir, falar e escrever sobre moderação de debates a partir de instruções passo a passo, assegurando equidade, tempo e clareza.

body: Esta aula treina **escrever frases claras e corretas (IELTS Writing, TOEFL Writing)**.

blocks.t: Toque em 🔊, ouça e repita cada palavra. Depois tente adivinhar o sentido.

blocks.title: How to Moderate a Public Debate
paras: **1. Agree the rules** in advance and **publish them**: speaking times, order, and how questions will be selected. **2. Open** by **welcoming** the audience, **introducing** the speakers briefly, and **stating** the motion. **3. Start the clock** visibly. **Cut off** politely but firmly: “**I must stop you there.**”

**4. Keep the exchange fair**: **alternate** speakers, **rein in** interruptions, and **ask the same kind of question** of both sides. **5. Press for evidence**, not for drama: “**What is your source for that figure?**” **6. Close** by **summarizing** points of agreement and disagreement; **never declare a winner** unless the format requires it. **Stay neutral**, even when provoked.

blocks.title: Match the word to its meaning

items.ans: And will you declare a winner

body: **I must stop you there.** — Preciso interrompê-lo aí.
**Keep to the point.** — Manter-se ao ponto.
**Stay on topic.** — Manter o assunto.
**Take turns.** — Revezar-se.
**Time is up.** — O tempo acabou.
**Hear both sides.** — Ouvir os dois lados.
**Fair and square.** — Justo e limpo.
**Keep the peace.** — Manter a paz.
**Draw to a close.** — Chegar ao fim.
**Level the playing field.** — Nivelar o campo.
**Yes, politely, but firmly.** — Sim, educadamente, mas com firmeza.
**And will you declare a winner?** — E vai declarar um vencedor?
**Will you cut speakers off when their time ends?** — Você vai interromper os oradores quando o tempo acabar?

blocks.task: Write 6 numbered steps for chairing a meeting or debate fairly, including one polite interruption formula.
blocks.model: 1. Circulate the agenda and rules beforehand. 2. Open by stating the purpose. 3. Keep a visible clock. 4. Alternate speakers and rein in interruptions. 5. If someone overruns, say, “I must stop you there.” 6. Summarize decisions and next steps before closing.
